text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Car bomb explodes in Birkhadem, southern district of Algiers, killing at least 10 people and wounding 20 others, two seriously. The blast came less than a week after the massacre of 32 civilians in Sid el Kebir village near Blida.
- Twelve companies and 43 units are offered for sale in 1996 but there was no interest from investors to buy them.
- Metal Sider offers 14,000 tonnes of sugar for sale.
- President Liamine Zeroual urges the government to implement cooperation accords reached during his tour in Bahrain, China, Vietnam and Qatar.
- More than 15 Belgian businessmen arrive in Algiers to discuss partnership and joint ventures with Algerians.
- The government adopts a state budget for 1997 to reconfigure tax system and crack down on tax fraud.
- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia presides over a mass meeting in Bab el Oued suburb to rally voters support for referendum to amend the constitution on November 28.
- Hachemi Cherif, leader of anti-Islamist Ettahadi party, says the proposed constitution favours political forces hostile to building a modern Algeria. He urges supporters to boycott the referendum.
